sections.title: Can this runbook be applied now?
paragraphs: Can you safely apply the cloud-managed model compute procedure from the supplied material? No. The operational procedure, provider documentation, expected result, and failure behavior are UNKNOWN, so they are omitted rather than guessed.

This resource is written at the intermediate level. It assumes that you can inspect a committed JSON resource, compare source records, and review a focused change, but it does not assume knowledge of any unnamed cloud service or tool.

sections.title: Correction procedure
paragraphs: Step 1: Obtain the exact committed contents and version-control history of the existing resource. If either cannot be obtained, stop the correction and recover the file and history from the authoritative repository rather than reconstructing them from the filename.

Step 2: Extract the old source title, publisher, URL, verification date, and the paragraphs that cite it. If the source record lacks an external URL or cannot be connected to specific paragraphs, mark the impact UNKNOWN and request the missing editorial provenance before changing guide content.

Step 3: Determine whether the old source moved, was replaced, or exceeded its review cadence, then check the applicable first-party HTTPS page. If the page cannot be opened or its publisher identity cannot be established, do not record a new verification date; obtain a network-enabled review or escalate the source for editorial replacement.

Step 4: Compare the verified source with only the claims and procedures that depended on the old record. If the comparison does not establish a correction, leave those passages unchanged. If it does establish one, edit only the affected passages and source metadata, and give each fallible operational step a supported next action.

Step 5: Validate that the resulting file is one syntactically valid JSON object and that each cited URL uses HTTPS. If JSON parsing fails, correct the serialization before committing. If an HTTPS URL does not resolve directly, replace it with a verified first-party page or leave the correction blocked.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is the recovered baseline resource, the old and current first-party source records, a dated source comparison, and a focused repository diff that changes only the source metadata and the claims or procedures the comparison proves were affected.

Verify the result by parsing the file as one JSON object, opening every listed HTTPS source, confirming each verification date records the actual review day, and comparing the corrected file with the recovered baseline. If any source cannot be opened, any affected claim cannot be traced, or unrelated prose changes appear in the diff, the correction has not passed verification and must not be committed.
That evidence is not present in the supplied material. The correction therefore remains blocked, and the operational expected result is UNKNOWN.
